title: Cathodoluminescence from Mn4+-Doped Fluorides
content: Alkali-metal- and alkaline-earth-metal-based fluorides, such as AF2 (A = Ca, Ba), ACF6 and B2CF6 (A = Na, K, Rb, Cs; B = Ca, Ba; C = Ti, Zr, Hf, Si, Ga, Ge, Sn) have been studied for future white LED devices and radiation detectors using Mn, transition metal and rare-earth metal dopants [1–8]. These phosphors are excellent host materials that absorb near-ultraviolet and blue light to exhibit narrow-band emissions from the dopants. Several studies reported for Mn4+-doped B2CF6 type hosts, where C is a single element [9–11]. Here, we report the synthesis of Mn4+-doped mixed matrix Cs2Zr0.5Sn0.5F6 by simple coprecipitation method and its cathodoluminescence (CL) study. In a typical synthesis, a solution of CsF, ZrO2, and SnF4 was separately prepared in 40% hydrofluoric (HF) acid. K2MnF6 was prepared following the protocol reported elsewhere and used as an Mn4+ precursor in the synthesis [1]. In a typical synthesizing procedure, the required ZrO2 and SnF4 solutions were mixed first and stirred for 30 min. Then, K2MnF6 was dissolved in 40% HF and added to the above solution. Afterward, CsF was added and precipitated with ethanol immediately. White precipitates were collected by centrifugation and washed with ethanol three times. The final product was dried at 70 °C to get white powders used for further studies.
